title: LinkedIn Loses Its Shortcut, Consent Comes Back Per Job | vitalii.no
description:
My job-apply bot used to let one button both approve a LinkedIn job and grant permission to explore its full application form -- a convenience, but it meant a single tap could commit to an application whose form the bot hadn't actually inspected yet. Meanwhile NAV and FINN jobs, which have far more predictable forms, were stuck waiting on that same manual gate, slowing down applications to the platforms where automation was actually safe.

I split trust by platform instead of collapsing it into one button, in a Telegram bot script. LinkedIn jobs now always require an explicit human review before any exploration or submission happens -- the single-button shortcut is gone. NAV and FINN jobs regain an auto-queue: once a listing scores above a threshold, the bot queues the application automatically, but the owner's final confirmation still gates the actual send.

LinkedIn applications now always get a human look before the bot touches the form, while NAV and FINN applications move through an automatic queue again -- trust is scoped to where it's actually earned, per platform and per job, instead of one shortcut covering everything.
